title: Extra $500,000 for Shelldale Crescent supportive housing
subtitle: Special meeting also covered the Home for Good campaign, CMHC deadline, Bill 23 costs and a tenant eviction concern.
overview: Council held a special meeting to decide on funding for the Kindle Communities supportive housing project at 10 Shelldale Crescent. It awarded an additional $500,000 from the Affordable Housing Reserve {{vote:m1}}. The money goes directly to Kindle Communities, and staff will update the funding agreements to set and monitor project criteria.

Staff said the project faced a $770,000 shortfall. The Home for Good campaign, run by the United Way and the Guelph Community Foundation, has committed to cover the remaining $270,000. The decision was time sensitive because of a commitment to the Canadian Mortgage and Housing Corporation, which had allowed a short extension past August 15.

For residents, the decision keeps a supportive housing project viable so people can be housed by the fall. It also uses the full amount Council set aside in the 2023 budget for the reserve. Staff said no other applications are expected this year, so a new request for proposals would wait until after the 2024 budget. Council also passed a routine by-law and adjourned.

decisions.detail: Council awarded an additional $500,000 from the Affordable Housing Reserve to Kindle Communities for the supportive housing project at 10 Shelldale Crescent {{vote:m1}}.
The City Solicitor and the Deputy Chief Administrative Officer of Public Services were directed to update and execute agreements with Kindle Communities to fund, outline and monitor project criteria.

debate: Staff recommended funding Kindle directly rather than through the Home for Good campaign. A matching-funds deadline could have left Kindle at risk of repaying the City, and Kindle had already completed the full request for proposals process.

Staff said the $500,000 equals the amount added to the Affordable Housing Reserve in the 2023 budget. They also said the amendment to Kindle's existing contribution agreement was similar to the earlier second round of funding for St. Joe's.
A delegate supported funding the project but compared its cost per unit with public subsidies that development fee waivers under Bill 23 could create, and asked for a public debate on those costs.
The same delegate raised concern about tenants being evicted from a sold apartment building on Carden Street and where they would find housing before winter.
Councillors thanked staff for acting quickly and urged the community to keep supporting the Home for Good campaign so the supportive housing units can be sustained.
